sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by confocal microscopy and flow cytometry in HEK293 cells (PMC5917007). Electrophysiology of the BBS-hERG1a-YFP construct itself was NOT MEASURED in the cited papers; however, the YFP C-terminal fusion and BBS insertion were used as the baseline 'WT' construct against which 16 LQT2 mutations were compared, implying the construct is functional. Electrophysiology of HA-tagged hERG in the same S1–S2 loop (at T443/E444) is confirmed unaffected by a separate study.
sites.rationale: The ledger line from PMC5917007 explicitly names T436/E437 as the junction, confirmed by a second independent ledger line from PMC10568093 ('placed between residues Thr436 and Glu437'). Python computation on the canonical 1159-aa sequence confirms position 436 = T and position 437 = E, both within the extracellular S1–S2 loop (topology landmarks 430–453). Distance from TM1 end (429): 7 residues; distance from TM2 start (454): 18 residues — both above the ≥3 threshold. C445 lies 9 residues C-terminal to the junction, well clear of the disulfide-forming cysteines. This is a distinct junction from the HA site at T443/E444 — two separate papers pin two separate junctions in the same loop, and both are reported. Ranked second because electrophysiology was not explicitly measured for the BBS construct (surface_only), whereas the HA construct at T443/E444 has explicit electrophysiology validation. A 13-residue bungarotoxin-binding site (BBS) was inserted between T436 and E437 in the extracellular S1–S2 loop of full-length hERG1a-YFP (BBS-hERG1a-YFP) using site-directed mutagenesis. Surface channels were labeled with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated bungarotoxin in non-permeabilized HEK293 cells. Robust surface expression was confirmed by confocal microscopy (YFP total pool, BTX647 surface pool) and flow cytometry (surface signal up to 100-fold above threshold). The construct was also used to study 16 LQT2 mutations in the PAS domain. Confirmed independently by PMC10568093 using the same T436/E437 junction. [validation: surface_only; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: A 13-residue bungarotoxin-binding site (BBS; TGGCGGTACTACGAGAGCAGCCTGGAGCCCTACCCCGAC) ( Sekine-Aizawa and Huganir, 2004 ; Yang et al., 2010 ) was then introduced between residues T436/E437 in the extracellular S1–S2 loop of hERG using the Quik-Change Lightning Site-Directed Mutagenesis Kit (Stratagene) according to the manufacturer's instructions. 16 LQT2 mutations were introduced in the PAS domain of BBS-hERG-YFP via site-directed mutagenesis.

sites.functional_impact_measured: Electrophysiology: tag stated not to affect electrophysiological properties (DOI:10.1101/2020.02.17.952606, citing Ficker et al. 2003). Surface expression confirmed by flow cytometry and confocal microscopy in non-permeabilized cells across multiple independent studies. Processing and function explicitly stated to be unaffected (PMC3861077: 'does not interfere with processing and function').
sites.rationale: The ledger line from DOI:10.1101/2020.02.17.952606 explicitly names T443 and E444 as the junction. Python computation on the canonical 1159-aa sequence confirms position 443 = T and position 444 = E, both within the extracellular S1–S2 loop (topology landmarks 430–453). Distance from TM1 end (429): 14 residues; distance from TM2 start (454): 11 residues — both well above the ≥3 threshold. C445 lies 2 residues C-terminal to the junction; however, the paper explicitly validates that this insertion does not affect electrophysiological properties, so the proximity is empirically tolerated. Multiple independent groups (PMC7704534, PMC3861077, PMC3877390, PMC13182972) have used the same HA-hERG construct for surface trafficking studies, all confirming surface display in non-permeabilized cells. Ranked first because surface_and_function validation is the highest level. A 9-amino-acid HA tag with flanking 4-aa linkers (NSEHYPYDVPDYAVTFE) was inserted between T443 and E444 in the extracellular S1–S2 loop of full-length KCNH2 (hERG1a) by inverse PCR. The construct was used in stable HEK293 cell lines. The tag was stated to have been demonstrated previously not to affect the electrophysiological properties of the channel. Surface expression was assessed by flow cytometry and confocal microscopy in multiple studies using this same HA-hERG construct (PMC7704534, PMC3861077, PMC3877390, PMC13182972). [validation: surface_and_function; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

literature_notes: Two distinct, residue-pinned insertion sites are supported by the ledger, both in the extracellular S1–S2 loop (topology 430–453) of KCNH2/hERG1a. Site 1 (T443/E444, HA tag) is ranked first because multiple papers confirm surface expression and electrophysiological function is preserved. Site 2 (T436/E437, BBS tag) is ranked second because surface expression is robustly confirmed but electrophysiology of the BBS construct itself was not explicitly reported in the cited papers. All other extracellular regions are either too short (S3–S4 loop: 501–501, 1 residue) or are the pore-turret region (S5–S6 loop: 571–638) for which no ledger evidence of tolerated insertions exists. The intracellular N-terminus (1–408) and C-terminus (657–1159) are not extracellular and were not considered. No ledger evidence supports any site outside the S1–S2 loop. The many papers citing 'HA tag in the first extracellular loop' without naming a residue (PMC7704534, PMC3861077, PMC3877390, PMC13182972) corroborate the loop-level evidence but do not add new junction positions beyond T443/E444 already pinned by DOI:10.1101/2020.02.17.952606.
